Hip Quiver.description: A leather case worn at the hip from a belt, holding arrows or crossbow bolts head-up for ready access. Common across medieval Europe for archers, hunters, and crossbowmen.

Belt.description: A strip of tanned leather fastened with an iron or bronze buckle, worn at the waist to gird a tunic, hang a purse, dagger, or keys. Status was shown through tooling, dyes, and metalwork.

Disguise Kit.description: A small case of cosmetics, false beards of human or horsehair, dyes, charcoal, mirrors and pieces of fabric used by spies, mummers and players to alter the appearance.

Telescope.description: A polished brass tube containing two ground glass lenses arranged to magnify distant objects. A rare and costly instrument prized by scholars, mariners and lords.

Nanobug.description: A pinhead-sized clockwork brooch fashioned by a master jeweller, set with tiny gears that buzz softly. A curious mechanical novelty rather than a useful tool.

Pickaxe.description: An iron-headed tool with a pointed pick on one end and a flat blade on the other, mounted on a wooden haft. Used by miners, sappers and quarrymen to break stone and ore.

Iron.description: A wrought iron ingot or bar of trade weight, the raw stock supplied to smiths for forging tools, weapons, nails and fittings.

Antibiotic.description: A jar of medicinal mould-and-honey poultice prepared by an apothecary, applied to wounds to stave off corruption and putrefaction. Folk medicine of monastic infirmaries.

Wooden.description: A simple wooden chest of plank construction, banded with iron straps and fitted with a hasp lock, used to store clothing, linens or household goods.

Piton.description: A short forged iron spike with an eyelet at one end, hammered into rock or timber as an anchor for ropes by climbers, sappers and besiegers.

VHF radio.description: A small tallow candle carried in a tin holder for travel, giving feeble light through one or two evenings of use.

Lights fire.description: A flint and steel striker with a pinch of charred linen tinder kept in a small pouch, used to kindle a fire by a quick stroke of steel against the flint's edge.

Acid (vial).description: A small stoppered glass vial of vitriol (aqua fortis) prepared by an alchemist, capable of corroding metal and burning flesh when poured or hurled.

Alchemist's Fire (flask).description: A clay or glass flask of sticky incendiary compound (naphtha and sulphur) sealed with wax. When broken upon a target it ignites and clings, burning fiercely.

Antitoxin (vial).description: A vial of theriac, a renowned medieval compound electuary of many herbs, opium and viper's flesh, taken as a remedy against poisons and venoms.

Ball Bearings (bag of 1000).description: A small drawstring sack containing one thousand small iron or lead spheres, scattered underfoot to trip pursuers or used by craftsmen as weights.

Barrel.description: A coopered cask of oak staves bound with iron hoops, used to store wine, ale, salt fish, flour or other goods. Stands about chest-high.

Basket.description: A handwoven basket of willow withies or rushes with a carrying handle, used to gather produce, carry bread, eggs or laundry.

Bedroll.description: A wool blanket and oiled canvas wrap that may be rolled and tied for travel, providing a sleeping place against the cold and wet of the road.

Bell.description: A small cast bronze hand-bell with a leather or wooden grip, rung to summon servants, attract attention, or warn of approach.

Book.description: A bound codex of vellum or parchment leaves protected by tooled leather covers over wooden boards, containing chronicles, tales, sermons or scholarly treatises.

Bottle, Glass.description: A small blown-glass bottle, usually of green or amber metal, stoppered with a cork or wax-sealed plug. Used for fine wine, oil, or apothecaries' tinctures.

Bucket.description: A coopered wooden bucket bound with iron or willow hoops, fitted with a rope or iron bail handle, used to carry water from well or stream.

Caltrops (bag of 20).description: A canvas pouch of twenty four-pronged iron caltrops, scattered upon the ground so that one spike points always upward to maim foot or hoof.

Chain (10 feet).description: Ten feet of forged iron chain of heavy oval links, used to secure prisoners, bind doors, draw buckets from wells, or moor a draught beast.

Chalk (1 piece).description: A small stick of natural chalk used to mark stone, slate or wood; favoured by masons, scribes and merchants for tallies.

Climber's Kit.description: A bundle of climbing equipment containing iron spikes, a hammer, hempen rope, a leather harness and gloves with hobnailed boot tips for ascending walls and cliffs.

Clothes, Common.description: A set of plain woollen tunic, hose, linen shirt, hood and shoes such as worn by peasants, labourers and servants throughout the medieval countryside.

Clothes, Fine.description: A noble's costume of dyed broadcloth, silk lining, fur trim and embroidered ornament, with hose, fitted gown and headdress, fit for court or feast.

Clothes, Traveler's.description: Sturdy woollen and leather garments for the road: a hooded cloak, padded tunic, breeches, hose and stout shoes proof against wind and weather.

Component Pouch.description: A small leather belt pouch divided into compartments, holding herbs, salts, powders, feathers and other natural reagents required by hedge-magicians and apothecaries.

Crowbar.description: A forged iron bar with a hooked, flattened end, used to lever open crates, prise nails, force doors and shift heavy stones.

Crystal (Arcane Focus).description: A polished crystal of clear quartz or coloured stone, set on a pendant or wand, used by hedge-witches and learned mages as a focus to channel arcane workings.

Orb (Arcane Focus).description: A polished sphere of clear or smoky glass, sometimes of rock crystal, mounted in a clawed metal stand and used as a scrying focus by sorcerers.

Rod (Arcane Focus).description: A short, thick rod of dark wood or metal, often capped with a gem at one or both ends, carried as an arcane focus and a mark of magical office.

Staff (Arcane Focus).description: A tall wooden walking-staff carved with runes and bound with iron, doubling as a scholar's traveling aid and a focus through which magic is shaped.

Wand (Arcane Focus).description: A slender carved wand of yew, ash or hazelwood about a foot long, sometimes tipped with metal or bone, used by mages as a focus for spells.

Sprig of Mistletoe (Druidic Focus).description: A fresh-cut sprig of mistletoe, gathered with a golden sickle in the old druidic manner. Sacred to forest priests and used as a focus for nature magic.

Totem (Druidic Focus).description: A small carved wooden token bearing the likeness of a sacred animal or natural symbol, hung from the belt or neck and used as a druidic focus.

Wooden Staff (Druidic Focus).description: A natural staff of seasoned oak, ash or rowan, sometimes still bearing its bark, carried by a druid as both walking aid and focus for the green magic.

Yew Wand (Druidic Focus).description: A short wand cut from a churchyard yew, used by druids and witches as a focus for nature magic and divination.

Amulet (Holy Symbol).description: A holy symbol of cast pewter or silver, depicting the cross, hammer or sigil of a saint or god, worn upon a cord or chain about the neck.

Emblem (Holy Symbol).description: A holy symbol embroidered in coloured silks or appliqued upon a tabard, banner or shield, declaring its bearer's faith and patronage.

Reliquary (Holy Symbol).description: A small ornamented box or pendant of gilt silver or carved bone, containing a fragment of bone, cloth or wood from a saint, carried as a holy symbol.

Fishing Tackle.description: A wooden rod with a horsehair or silken line, corkwood floats, bone or iron hooks, lead weights and a small net, used by fishers along rivers and lakes.

Grappling Hook.description: A forged iron hook with three or four curved prongs and a ring for tying rope, hurled to catch upon walls, ledges or rigging and so anchor a climb.

Hammer.description: A simple iron-headed claw or peen hammer mounted on a wooden haft, used by carpenters, smiths and travellers to drive nails, pitons and stakes.

Hammer, Sledge.description: A heavy two-handed maul with a square iron head on a long wooden haft, used to break stone, drive large stakes or batter open doors.

Healer's Kit.description: A leather satchel containing linen bandages, a small knife, needle and silk thread, splints, salves of comfrey and honey, and other simples for binding wounds.

Holy Water (flask).description: A small glass or pewter flask of water that has been blessed by a priest at the font, used in rites of exorcism and against unholy creatures.

Hourglass.description: Two pear-shaped glass bulbs joined at the neck and set in a wooden frame, in which fine sand passes from one bulb to the other to mark a known span of time.

Hunting Trap.description: A spring-jawed iron trap with toothed jaws and a chain, set upon the ground and concealed beneath leaves to seize the leg of bear, wolf, or unwary man.

Ink (1 ounce bottle).description: A small earthen or glass bottle of iron-gall ink, made from oak galls, vitriol, gum arabic and wine, used by scribes for writing on parchment.

Ink Pen.description: A goose- or swan-quill cut and slit by penknife to a sharp nib, the standard writing instrument of medieval scribes and clerks.

Ladder (10-foot).description: A simple ladder of two stout pine rails joined by ten cross rungs, ten feet in length, used by builders, orchard-keepers and besiegers.

Lamp.description: A small open or covered oil lamp of pottery or brass with a wick of twisted flax, fed with olive or animal oil to give a steady flame.

Lantern, Bullseye.description: A tin or brass lantern fitted with a thick convex glass lens at the front that focuses the candle's light into a directional beam, with shutters to mask it.

Lantern, Hooded.description: A pierced tin lantern with horn or glass panes and a hinged hood that may be lowered to dim the light, hung from a hook or carried by a ring.

Lock.description: A keyed warded iron lock such as a smith might forge for a chest or door, opened with its matching iron key or, more difficultly, with picks.

Magnifying Glass.description: A ground glass lens set in a turned wooden or bone handle, used by scholars and jewellers to read fine writing or examine small objects.

Manacles.description: A pair of forged iron wrist shackles joined by a short chain and closed with a keyed lock, used to restrain prisoners.

Mess Kit.description: A small tinned-iron box containing a cup, plate, wooden spoon and bone-handled knife, the simple eating gear of a soldier or pilgrim on the road.

Mirror, Steel.description: A small disc of polished and tinned steel set in a leather-bound wooden frame, giving a dim but clear reflection. Mirrors of true silvered glass were rare and very dear.

Oil (flask).description: A clay or glass flask of olive or rendered animal oil, sealed with a wax-corked stopper, burnt in lamps or poured upon waters and floors as fuel.

Paper (one sheet).description: A single sheet of rag-pulp paper, a costly novelty from Italian or Iberian mills, used for letters, ledgers and account books.

Parchment (one sheet).description: A single sheet of parchment scraped, stretched and dressed from the skin of a sheep or calf, the chief writing surface of medieval Europe.

Perfume (vial).description: A small glass or alabaster vial of scented water, distilled from roses, lavender or musk, used to mask the odours of person and chamber.

Pick, Miner's.description: A heavy single-pointed iron pick on a stout wooden haft, swung two-handed by miners to break ore from rock face in tunnel and quarry.

Poison, Basic (vial).description: A small stoppered vial of black hellebore, hemlock or wolfsbane decoction, smeared upon a blade or arrowhead to sicken a wound.

Pole (10-foot).description: A straight ash or pine pole some ten feet long, used to test soft ground, sound water depth, prop a tarp, or push at out-of-reach things.

Pot, Iron.description: A heavy cast or wrought iron pot with a bail handle, used over hearth or campfire to boil pottage, stew meat or render fat.

Potion of Healing.description: A small stoppered vial of red liquid prepared by an apothecary or alchemist from herbs and rare reagents, which knits flesh and restores vigour when drunk.

Pouch.description: A small leather or stout cloth pouch closed with a drawstring or buckle flap, hung from belt or thong to carry coins, flint and steel, or trinkets.

Quiver.description: A leather case worn at the back, hip or saddle, holding up to twenty arrows or crossbow bolts ready to the archer's hand.

Ram, Portable.description: A stout oak beam shod with iron at one end and fitted with rope or chain handles for two or four men, used to batter down barred doors.

Rations (1 day).description: A day's worth of travel food: salt pork or jerky, hardtack or rye biscuit, a wedge of hard cheese, dried fruit, and a handful of nuts wrapped in linen.

Robes.description: Long, loose woollen or linen garments reaching to the ankle, worn by clerics, scholars, monks and judges over an undertunic.

Rope, Hempen (50 feet).description: Fifty feet of three-strand hempen rope of about half an inch thickness, the workhorse cordage of medieval ports, mines, gallows and farms.

Rope, Silk (50 feet).description: Fifty feet of fine plaited silken rope, lighter and stronger for its weight than hemp; an expensive luxury rope used by acrobats and infiltrators.

Sack.description: A coarse hempen or linen sack with a drawstring mouth, used to carry grain, wool, vegetables or loot in great quantity.

Scale, Merchant's.description: A small balance with two brass pans suspended on cords from a wooden or iron beam, with a set of standard weights for measuring coin, spice or precious metal.

Sealing Wax.description: A stick of hard red wax, sometimes scented with cinnabar or musk, melted by candle flame and dripped upon a folded letter to receive a signet's impression.

Signal Whistle.description: A small whistle of carved bone, brass or boxwood, used by shepherds, watchmen, boatswains and hunt-masters to send simple signals over distance.

Signet Ring.description: A heavy gold, silver or bronze ring engraved in intaglio with a personal device or coat of arms, pressed into hot wax to authenticate letters and seals.

Spellbook.description: A leather-bound tome upon wooden boards, containing a hundred leaves of parchment closely written in a wizard's hand with arcane formulae, sigils and notes.

Spike, Iron (10).description: A bundle of ten short forged iron spikes some six inches long, hammered between flagstones, into door jambs or under wedges to fix things in place.

Spyglass.description: A draw-tube of brass and leather containing two glass lenses, magnifying distant objects two- or three-fold. A precious instrument of mariners and lords.

Tent, Two-Person.description: A simple ridge tent of waxed canvas with two stout poles, guy ropes and iron pegs, sheltering two travellers against rain and wind.

Tinderbox.description: A small tinned-iron box containing a flint, a bowed steel striker and a wad of charred linen tinder, used to kindle a fire by sparks struck onto the tinder.

Vial.description: A small stoppered glass vial holding about four ounces of liquid, used by apothecaries and alchemists to keep tinctures, oils and reagents.

Waterskin.description: A bag of stitched goat- or pigskin sealed with pitch, holding about four pints of water, ale or wine and slung from belt or shoulder for the road.

Burglar's Pack.description: A backpack containing a bag of ball bearings, ten feet of string, a small bell, five candles, a crowbar, a hammer, ten pitons, a hooded lantern, two flasks of oil, five days of rations, a tinderbox, a waterskin, and fifty feet of hempen rope.

Diplomat's Pack.description: A chest containing two map cases, a set of fine clothes, a bottle of ink, an ink pen, a lamp, two flasks of oil, five sheets of paper, a vial of perfume, sealing wax, and a cake of soap.

Dungeoneer's Pack.description: A backpack containing a crowbar, a hammer, ten pitons, ten torches, a tinderbox, ten days of rations, a waterskin, and fifty feet of hempen rope strapped to the side.

Entertainer's Pack.description: A backpack containing a bedroll, two costumes, five candles, five days of rations, a waterskin, and a disguise kit, suited to a travelling minstrel or mummer.

Explorer's Pack.description: A backpack containing a bedroll, a mess kit, a tinderbox, ten torches, ten days of rations, a waterskin, and fifty feet of hempen rope strapped to the side.

Priest's Pack.description: A backpack containing a blanket, ten candles, a tinderbox, an alms box, two blocks of incense, a censer, vestments, two days of rations, and a waterskin.

Scholar's Pack.description: A backpack containing a book of lore, a bottle of ink, an ink pen, ten sheets of parchment, a little bag of sand for blotting, and a small knife.

Alchemist's Supplies.description: A wooden case fitted with a small bronze alembic, glass retorts and vials, mortar and pestle, brass weights and a selection of common reagents for distilling and compounding.

Brewer's Supplies.description: A set of brewing tools including a copper mash kettle, oak fermenting tub, paddles, hops bag, hydrometer-stick and bungs, used to brew beer and ale.

Calligrapher's Supplies.description: A wooden case containing fine quills, penknife, several inks of black, red and green, gold leaf, gum arabic, parchment and a ruler, for the production of ornate writing.

Carpenter's Tools.description: A roll holding a saw, hammer, mallet, chisels of several sizes, an auger, a brace and bit, a plane, a try-square and nails, used to shape and join timber.

Cartographer's Tools.description: A leather case of fine quills, inks, brushes, pigments, set-square, compasses, ruler, and rolls of parchment, used by mapmakers to draft and copy charts.

Cobbler's Tools.description: A roll of cordwainer's tools including iron lasts, a curved knife, awls, waxes, hammer, pincers, hemp thread and bristle needles, for making and mending shoes.

Cook's Utensils.description: A roll of cooking gear holding an iron pot, a skillet, a meat hook, ladle, knives of several sizes, a pestle, salt-box and wooden spoons.

Glassblower's Tools.description: An iron blowpipe, marver block, jacks, shears, blocks and pucellas used to gather molten glass from the furnace and shape it into vessels.

Jeweler's Tools.description: A small case of fine files, gravers, tweezers, pliers, loupe, mandrels, pitch bowl, and tiny crucibles for setting stones and crafting jewelry.

Leatherworker's Tools.description: A roll of awls, a half-moon knife, edgers, stitching needles, waxed thread, hammers and a small marble slab, used to cut and stitch leather goods.

Mason's Tools.description: A bag of stoneworking gear: a trowel, a mallet, a set of cold chisels and points, a plumb-bob, a square and a measuring cord, for dressing stone and laying mortar.

Painter's Supplies.description: Paints, brushes, and canvases used to create paintings and frescoes.

Potter's Tools.description: Wheels, knives, and shaping tools used to craft ceramics and pottery.

Smith's Tools.description: Hammers, tongs, and bellows used at a forge to work metal.

Tinker's Tools.description: Bits of metal, small tools, and components used to repair small mechanisms.

Weaver's Tools.description: Needles, thread, and a small loom used to make and mend fabric.

Woodcarver's Tools.description: Knives, gouges, and chisels used to carve and shape wood.

Dice Set.description: A set of small bone or wooden dice used for games of chance.

Dragonchess Set.description: A three-tiered chess variant played by scholars and nobles.

Playing Card Set.description: A deck of fifty-two illustrated cards used for various card games.

Three-Dragon Ante Set.description: A deck of cards depicting dragons, used to play the popular gambling game.

Bagpipes.description: An air-filled bag with pipes used to play traditional folk music.

Dulcimer.description: A trapezoidal stringed instrument played by striking strings with hammers.

Flute.description: A long wooden tube with finger holes producing music when blown across.

Lute.description: A pear-shaped stringed instrument popular among bards and minstrels.

Lyre.description: A small harp-like stringed instrument plucked or strummed.

Horn.description: A curved horn instrument used to signal or play simple tunes.

Pan Flute.description: A series of small pipes bound together producing a haunting whistle when blown.

Shawm.description: A double-reed wind instrument with a bright, piercing sound.

Viol.description: A bowed stringed instrument played upright between the knees.

Forgery Kit.description: A small box of pens, inks, papers, parchments, lead sheets, and sealing wax for creating forged documents.

Herbalism Kit.description: A pouch with clippers, mortar and pestle, pouches, and vials for harvesting and applying herbs.

Navigator's Tools.description: A sextant, compass, calipers, ruler, and other tools used to navigate at sea.

Plumb Bob.description: Lead weight on a string used to establish the vertical when building.

Mason's Square.description: Right-angled iron rule used by masons and carpenters to ensure square corners.

Plough (Heavy Wheeled).description: Wheeled mouldboard plough with coulter, drawn by oxen, that cuts and turns heavy soil.

Plough (Light Scratch).description: Lighter ard or scratch plough used in dry Mediterranean soils.

Harrow.description: Wooden frame set with iron teeth, dragged over ploughed land to break clods.

Ox Yoke.description: Heavy carved wooden beam fitted to a pair of oxen so they may draw together.

Sickle.description: Curved iron blade with short wooden handle for reaping cereal crops.

Scythe.description: Long-handled curved blade for mowing grass and grain.

Winnowing Fan.description: Flat shovel-like tool used to toss threshed grain so chaff blows away.

Pitchfork.description: Two-tined wooden fork for tossing hay and sheaves.

Spade (Iron-Shod).description: Wooden spade with iron edge for digging and turning earth.

Mattock.description: Heavy hoe with one broad blade and one pick blade for breaking hard ground.

Hoe.description: Long-handled tool with iron blade at right angle for weeding and tilling.

Pruning Hook.description: Curved billhook on a long handle for pruning vines and trees.

Beehive (Skep).description: Conical straw-coiled basket used as a beehive, kept on a board near the orchard.

Beekeeper's Veil.description: Cloth veil worn over the head and shoulders to protect the beekeeper from stings.

Fish Trap (Weir).description: Wooden lattice trap set in a stream to funnel fish into a basket.

Hand Mill.description: Domestic rotary millstone used by villagers when avoiding the lord's mill.

Cart (Two-Wheeled).description: Two-wheeled wooden cart drawn by an ox or horse for hauling loads.

Wagon (Four-Wheeled).description: Heavier four-wheeled wooden wagon for long-distance hauling of goods.

Sledge.description: Wheel-less wooden runner-sled used to drag heavy loads over earth or snow.

Wine Press.description: Heavy wooden screw press for crushing grapes to extract wine must.

Olive Press.description: Heavy wooden lever-and-screw press for extracting oil from olives.

Cider Press.description: Wooden screw press for crushing apples to make cider.

Wine Cask.description: Oak barrel of standard size for storing and transporting wine.

Tun.description: Very large oak barrel holding 252 gallons of wine, the standard merchant unit.

Hogshead.description: Cask holding 63 gallons of wine, beer, or other liquid.

Sack of Flour.description: Hempen sack containing one bushel of milled flour.

Sack of Salt.description: Hempen sack of coarse salt from the salt-pans of the Bay of Bourgneuf or Lüneburg.

Bolt of Linen.description: Roll of woven linen cloth, the everyday fabric of shirts and shifts.

Bolt of Wool Cloth.description: Roll of woven woolen cloth, sturdy and warm, dyed and finished.

Bolt of Silk.description: Roll of woven silk imported from Byzantium, Sicily or Andalusia.

Bolt of Samite.description: Heavy silk fabric interwoven with gold threads.

Cloth-of-Gold.description: Cloth woven with strips of beaten gold, the most luxurious fabric known.

Ermine Pelts.description: White winter fur of the stoat, used to trim royal and noble robes.

Vair (Squirrel Fur).description: Grey-and-white squirrel fur sewn in heraldic patterns to line winter robes.

Sable Fur.description: Black-brown fur of the sable, prized above all furs save ermine.

Saffron.description: Dried stigmas of the crocus, the most expensive spice by weight, used in cookery and medicine.

Black Pepper.description: Dried peppercorns of Piper nigrum imported from India by Venetian merchants.

Cinnamon.description: Bark of the cinnamon tree, sold rolled into quills.

Ginger.description: Dried ginger root, used in spiced wines and cookery.

Cloves.description: Dried flower buds of the clove tree, intensely aromatic.

Nutmeg.description: Dried seed of the nutmeg tree, grated for spice.

Cardamom.description: Aromatic green seedpods imported from southern India.

Galangal.description: Pungent root similar to ginger, popular in medieval cookery.

Grains of Paradise.description: Peppery West African seeds used as substitute for pepper.

Ambergris.description: Waxy grey substance from the sperm whale, used in perfumery and medicine.

Civet.description: Musky paste collected from the civet cat, used in perfumes.

Musk.description: Strong-scented secretion from the musk deer, the most prized perfume base.

Rosewater.description: Distilled water of damask roses, used to flavor food and perfume the hands.

Sugar Loaf.description: Cone of refined cane sugar imported from Cyprus or Sicily.

Honey Pot.description: Glazed earthenware pot of strained honey from a beekeeper's hives.

Beeswax Block.description: Cake of refined beeswax used for candles, sealing, and waterproofing.

Olive Oil Amphora.description: Tall earthenware jar of olive oil from Provence or Iberia.

Almonds (Sack).description: Sack of shelled almonds from Spain or Sicily, used in cookery and medicine.

Dried Figs (Basket).description: Basket of dried figs from the Mediterranean, sweet and long-keeping.

Dates (Basket).description: Basket of dried dates from North Africa or the Levant.

Raisins (Sack).description: Sack of dried grapes from Iberia or Greece.

Wheaten Loaf.description: Loaf of fine white wheat bread, the food of the wealthy.

Maslin Loaf.description: Loaf of bread made from mixed wheat and rye flour.

Rye Loaf.description: Dark dense loaf of rye bread, common in northern Europe.

Cheese Wheel.description: Aged round of hard cheese from the dairy.

Salt Pork (Barrel).description: Barrel of pork pieces preserved in brine for winter use.

Smoked Bacon Side.description: Side of bacon smoked and hung in the rafters, slowly used through the winter.

Salt Cod (Stockfish).description: Air-dried salted cod from Norway or Iceland, hard as wood, soaked before eating.

Pickled Herring (Barrel).description: Barrel of herring pickled in salt and vinegar, the staple Lenten fish of the north.

Pomegranate.description: Imported pomegranate fruit, prized in Iberia and Sicily.

Verjuice (Bottle).description: Sour juice of unripe grapes, used as cooking acid.

Vinegar (Cask).description: Cask of wine vinegar used for preserving and flavoring.

Mustard Pot.description: Pot of ground mustard mixed with vinegar, condiment of the medieval table.

Wine Skin.description: Stitched goatskin bag for carrying wine on the road.

Leather Bottle.description: Stiffened leather bottle (costrel) carried at the belt or on a strap.

Palfrey.description: Smooth-gaited riding horse favored by ladies and clerics for travel.

Courser.description: Light fast horse used for hunting and skirmishing.

Destrier.description: Heavy stallion war-horse trained to charge in battle, the prized mount of knights.

Rouncey.description: Sturdy general-purpose riding horse for ordinary travel and light cavalry.

Hackney.description: Hired horse for shorter trips, often poor quality.

Sumpter (Pack Horse).description: Pack horse of stout build for carrying baggage on the road.

Mule.description: Sterile cross of horse and ass, sure-footed and strong, valued for mountain travel.

Ass (Donkey).description: Small sturdy beast of burden carrying goods or pulling small carts for the poor.

Milk Cow.description: Dairy cow yielding milk, butter, and cheese for the household.

Ewe.description: Female sheep yielding wool and milk, the foundation of the medieval economy.

Wether.description: Castrated male sheep raised for fine wool and meat.

Sow.description: Female pig kept for breeding and meat, foraging in woods and yards.

Hen.description: Domestic hen yielding eggs and eventually meat for the cottage.

Capon.description: Castrated cockerel fattened for the table, prized for its tender flesh.

Goose.description: Domestic goose kept for meat, eggs, and feathers.

Dovecote (Pigeons).description: Tall stone or wood structure housing pigeons that supply meat all year for the lord.

Hawk (Goshawk).description: Trained female goshawk for hawking small game, fitted with hood and bells.

Falcon (Peregrine).description: Trained peregrine falcon for hawking from horseback, the gentleman's bird.

Gerfalcon.description: Largest of the falcons, white northern bird reserved by custom for kings.

Sparrowhawk.description: Small hawk used by ladies and priests to hunt small birds.

Greyhound.description: Slim swift hunting dog used to course hares and deer.

Alaunt.description: Heavy boar-hunting dog of great strength and courage.

Lymer (Tracking Hound).description: Bloodhound trained to follow a deer's scent silently on a leash.

Falconer's Glove.description: Heavy leather gauntlet protecting the falconer's hand from his bird's talons.

Hawk Hood.description: Small leather cap that blinds the hawk to keep it calm when not hunting.

Hawk Bells.description: Tiny brass bells fitted to the hawk's legs to track its position.

Saddle (Riding).description: Wood-tree leather saddle for riding, with stirrups and girth.

War Saddle.description: High-cantled saddle locking the rider in place during the charge.

Side Saddle (Pillion).description: Padded saddle behind the rider on which a lady sits sideways.

Pack Saddle.description: Wooden frame saddle for carrying loads on a sumpter horse or mule.

Horseshoes (Set of 4).description: Iron horseshoes nailed to the hooves to protect them on hard roads.

Currycomb.description: Toothed iron comb used to clean a horse's coat.

Horse Brush.description: Stiff bristled brush used after the currycomb to smooth the coat.

Horse Blanket.description: Heavy wool blanket draped over horse in cold weather.

Caparison.description: Decorated cloth cover draping a destrier with the knight's heraldry.

Stirrup.description: Iron foot-loops hung from the saddle giving the rider a secure stance.

Spurs.description: Pricked iron heel-pieces for guiding a horse, marker of knightly status.

Hay Bale.description: Bound bundle of dried hay for fodder.

Sack of Oats.description: Hempen sack of oats, used as horse fodder and for making porridge.

Windlass.description: Hand-cranked spool used to lift heavy loads via rope, fitted on wells and over pits.

Treadwheel Crane.description: Large wooden wheel walked by men inside, lifting heavy stones in cathedral construction.

Drawbridge Chain.description: Heavy iron chain pair raising the timber drawbridge across a moat.

Portcullis.description: Heavy iron-shod oak grille that drops to seal a gateway against attack.

Murder Hole Grating.description: Iron grille covering an opening above a gate-passage through which boiling oil is poured.

Iron-Bound Door.description: Heavy oak door reinforced with iron straps for the gatehouse or keep.

Coffer.description: Smaller wooden chest for personal possessions, often with elaborate ironwork.

Trestle Table.description: Long board set on trestles for dining; struck and stored after the meal.

Bench.description: Long wooden bench for seating diners along the trestle.

Joint Stool.description: Sturdy four-legged wooden stool for individual seating.

High Chair (Lord's).description: Carved wooden chair with high back and arms, reserved for the master of the house.

Bed (Tester).description: Curtained bed with carved frame, hangings, mattress, sheets and coverlet.

Pallet Bed.description: Straw-stuffed mattress laid on the floor for servants and the poor.

Feather Mattress.description: Tick stuffed with goose feathers, the luxury bedding of the wealthy.

Wool Blanket.description: Heavy woven wool blanket for the bed.

Linen Sheet.description: Pair of linen bedsheets, white and finely woven.

Tapestry.description: Woven hanging depicting biblical or chivalric scenes, hung on hall walls.

Floor Rushes.description: Cut sweet-smelling rushes strewn on the hall floor, replaced periodically.

Brazier.description: Iron pan on legs holding charcoal embers to warm a chamber.

Chamber Pot.description: Glazed ceramic pot used at night, emptied by servants in the morning.

Garderobe Bench.description: Wooden bench seat over a stone shaft in a castle for relieving oneself.

Wash Tub.description: Wooden tub for washing clothes or bathing.

Soap (Castile).description: Hard white olive-oil soap from Spain, mild and prized for fine linens and bathing.

Soft Soap.description: Yellow-brown semi-liquid soap of tallow and lye, common for laundry.

Comb (Ivory).description: Carved double-sided comb of ivory or boxwood for hair and beard.

Mirror (Polished Metal).description: Small disc of polished bronze or steel used for grooming.

Mirror (Glass).description: Small glass mirror backed with lead, expensive new technology from Venice.

Toothpick.description: Small silver, bone or wooden pick for cleaning teeth, often hung from the belt.

Surgeon's Kit.description: Roll holding scalpel, lancet, probe, and tweezers used by physicians and barber-surgeons.

Cupping Glass.description: Small glass globe heated and applied to skin to draw blood for medical bleeding.

Urine Flask.description: Pear-shaped glass flask used by physicians to inspect a patient's urine for diagnosis.

Theriac Pot.description: Sealed pot of theriac, the multi-ingredient panacea, prepared in Venice and Genoa.

Mithridate.description: Antidotal electuary of many ingredients used as cure-all and poison antidote.

Chess Set.description: Carved bone or wood chess pieces with a wooden board, the noble's pastime.

Tables (Backgammon Set).description: Folding wooden board with carved counters and dice for the popular tables game.

Dice (Pair).description: Pair of bone or ivory dice for gaming and gambling.

Playing Cards.description: Hand-painted parchment cards, very rare in 1220 (just arriving from the East).

Harp.description: Triangular wooden harp with horsehair or gut strings, played by bards.

Vielle (Fiddle).description: Bowed five-stringed predecessor of the violin, played by jongleurs.

Recorder.description: End-blown wooden flute with finger holes.

Tabor (Drum).description: Small two-headed drum hung at hip and beaten with a stick.

Pipe (Tabor Pipe).description: One-handed three-holed flute played alongside a tabor.

Hurdy-Gurdy.description: Wheel-bowed stringed instrument with keyboard, played by mendicants.

Carillon Bells.description: Set of small tuned bells played with hammers, used in monasteries.

Habit (Monk's).description: Plain woolen robe with hood and cord belt worn by monks of the Benedictine rule.

Tonsure Razor.description: Special razor for shaving the crown of a cleric's head.

Scapular.description: Long woolen panel worn front and back over the habit.

Mendicant Friar's Cord.description: Knotted rope belt of a Franciscan friar, with three knots for the vows.

Hair Shirt.description: Coarse haircloth garment worn against the skin as bodily mortification.

Discipline (Scourge).description: Knotted-cord whip used by religious for self-mortification.

Pyx Pendant (Lay).description: Small lockable container worn around the neck holding a relic or piece of consecrated host.

Agnus Dei.description: Wax disc impressed with the Lamb of God, blessed by the Pope and worn as amulet.

Pilgrim Flask (Ampulla).description: Lead pewter flask of holy water or oil from a pilgrimage shrine, worn around the neck.

Coopered Bucket.description: Wooden bucket made of staves and hoops, with a rope handle for drawing water.

Rope (50 ft).description: Coil of fifty feet of stout hempen rope for general use.

Hempen Cord.description: Spool of light hempen cord for tying, sewing sacks, and lacing.

Leather Strap.description: Yard of cut leather for binding and harness-making.

Iron Nails (100).description: Hundred forged iron nails of various sizes for carpentry.

Glass Window Pane (Small).description: Small leaded glass pane for a domestic window, formed of small quarries soldered together.

Stained Glass Quarry.description: Single piece of colored stained glass for inserting in a church window.

Lead Cames.description: Lead H-channels used to hold pieces of stained glass together in windows.

Brick (Hundred).description: Hundred fired clay bricks for building.

Roof Tile (Hundred).description: Hundred fired clay roof tiles for covering houses.

Slate (Hundred).description: Hundred quarried roofing slates from Wales or Anjou.

Lime (Sack).description: Sack of slaked lime for mortar and whitewash.

Pitch (Cake).description: Cake of pitch used for caulking ships and sealing barrels.

Iron Bar (Stockholm).description: Bar of high-quality wrought iron from Sweden, traded by the Hanseatic League.

Tin Ingot.description: Cast ingot of Cornish or Bohemian tin, used by pewterers and bronze-founders.

Lead Pig.description: Cast pig of lead from English or Saxon mines for plumbing and roofing.

Copper Ingot.description: Hammered ingot of copper for brass-making and roofing.

Quicksilver (Mercury).description: Liquid silvery metal used by alchemists and gilders, sold in stoppered flasks.

Brimstone (Sulphur).description: Lump of yellow brimstone used in alchemy, medicine, and incendiaries.

Saltpetre.description: Crystalline potassium nitrate scraped from cellar walls, used in alchemy and medicine.

Sal Ammoniac.description: Crystalline ammonium chloride imported from Egypt, used in alchemy and metalworking.

Verdigris.description: Green copper-acetate pigment scraped from copper plates exposed to vinegar.

Litharge.description: Yellow-orange lead oxide used by alchemists and glaziers.

Cinnabar.description: Red ore of mercury used as pigment and source of quicksilver.

Aqua Vitae (Bottle).description: Distilled spirit of wine, the alchemical 'water of life', used in medicine and alchemy.

Aqua Fortis (Nitric Acid).description: Strong corrosive distilled from saltpetre and vitriol, used by alchemists.

Vitriol.description: Blue or green crystalline copper or iron sulphate, used in alchemy and dyeing.

Alum.description: Astringent crystals from Phocaea (Anatolia), used in tanning, dyeing, and medicine.

Borax.description: White crystalline mineral imported from Tibet, used as flux in metalworking.

Gum Arabic.description: Hardened sap of acacia, dissolved in water for ink-making and gilding.

Beech Tablet.description: Smooth flat panel of beechwood prepared for tempera painting of icons or panels.

Egg Tempera Pot.description: Pot of egg-yolk and pigment tempera used for panel painting.

Brushes (Set).description: Set of pointed brushes of squirrel or marten hair set in quill ferrules.

Sigil Ring (Hermetic).description: Magus's signet ring engraved with his personal sigil, used to seal Hermetic correspondence.

Magus's Robes.description: Distinctive robes worn by Order of Hermes magi, often house-colored or covenant-colored.

House Bonisagus Cloak.description: Plain woolen cloak suitable for a Bonisagus magus dedicated to research.

Tribunal Token.description: Small carved or cast token marking a magus's right to attend Tribunal.

Lab Notebook (Blank).description: Bound parchment book with stitched binding, blank for laboratory notes.

Lab Stool.description: Tall wooden stool allowing the experimenter to work at his bench.

Lab Bench.description: Sturdy oak workbench with iron-bound corners for laboratory operations.

Lab Shelves.description: Set of fitted oak shelving holding jars, bottles, and books.

Glass Beaker.description: Cylindrical glass vessel with pouring lip for measuring and mixing.

Glass Flask (Round).description: Round-bottomed glass flask for boiling reagents over a flame.

Iron Cauldron (Lab).description: Small iron cauldron for boiling and reducing decoctions in the laboratory.

Brass Mortar.description: Heavy brass mortar with iron pestle for grinding hard substances.

Apothecary Cabinet.description: Tall wooden cabinet with many small labeled drawers holding herbs and reagents.

Drying Rack.description: Wooden frame with cross-pieces for drying herbs and roots in bunches.

Hand Lens (Reading Stone).description: Hemisphere of polished beryl or rock crystal used to magnify writing.

Spectacles.description: Pair of riveted convex lenses held to the nose, very recent invention from Italy.

Sundial (Portable).description: Pocket-sized engraved brass sundial that folds for travel.

Folk Charm Bag.description: Small linen bag of herbs, hair clippings, and inscribed bone for folk-magic protection.

Witch's Distaff.description: Cleft staff of rowan, sometimes mistaken for a folk-magical instrument by villagers.

Hagstone.description: Stone with naturally occurring hole, hung up for protection against witches.

Horseshoe (Hung).description: Old horseshoe nailed over the door for luck and as guard against the fey.

Witch Bottle.description: Sealed pottery jar holding pins, hair, and urine, buried under the threshold for protection.

Cunning Woman's Kit.description: Wicker basket containing herbs, pins, twine, and minor charms used by a cunning woman.

Divining Rod.description: Forked hazel rod cut on Midsummer Eve, used to divine for water or metal.

Ash Walking Staff.description: Stout staff of ash wood, considered protection against the fey on lonely roads.

Iron Horseshoe Nails.description: Iron nails carried in pocket as protection against the fey.

Salt Crock.description: Pottery jar of salt, scattered to ward off evil spirits at thresholds.

Rowan Cross.description: Small cross woven from rowan twigs and bound with red thread, hung against witches.

Herbal Sachet.description: Linen bundle of dried herbs (rue, vervain, St John's wort) hung against ill-wishing.

Coin (Silver Penny).description: Standard silver penny minted across England, France, and the Empire.

Coin (Gold Florin).description: Florentine gold coin newly struck (from 1252 in canon, anachronistic for 1220 but anticipated).

Coin (Bezant).description: Byzantine gold solidus circulating in Mediterranean trade.

Tally Stick.description: Notched wooden stick split between debtor and creditor as record of a debt.

Counting Board (Abacus).description: Lined wooden board on which counters are moved to perform calculations.

Merchant's Ledger.description: Bound paper or parchment book in which a merchant records accounts.

Steelyard (Roman Balance).description: Single-armed weighing scale with sliding counterweight, used in markets.

Bushel Measure.description: Sealed wooden tub of standard volume used to measure grain in markets.

Yard-Stick.description: Iron-tipped wooden rod of one yard length for measuring cloth.

Merchant's Strongbox.description: Heavy iron-bound chest used to transport coin, often with multiple locks.

Pack-Saddle Bag.description: Pair of large leather panniers slung either side of a sumpter horse.

Travelling Chest.description: Sturdy wooden chest with rope handles for travel by cart or pack-train.

Map (Mappa Mundi).description: Painted parchment world map showing Jerusalem at center, often with marvels and beasts.

Portolan Chart.description: Painted sailor's chart of coastlines marked with rhumb lines and ports.

Hour Glass (Sand-Clock).description: Large half-hour or hour sandglass used aboard ship and in monasteries.

Water Clock (Clepsydra).description: Bronze water-flow timekeeping vessel marked with hours, used in monasteries.

Pilgrim Flask.description: A small lead or pewter ampulla worn on a cord around the neck, filled with holy water or oil from a shrine.

Costrel.description: A leather or wooden flask with side loops for a strap, used by pilgrims and travelers to carry wine or water.

Bota Bag.description: A pear-shaped wineskin of pitched leather with a horn or wooden spout, common across Iberia.

Demijohn.description: A large bulbous glass bottle protected by a wicker basket, used for storing wine, oil, or vinegar.

Stone Crock.description: A glazed earthenware jar with a wide mouth, used to keep butter, lard, or pickled foods.

Salt Cellar.description: An ornate footed dish set on the high table, marking rank: those seated 'above the salt' enjoyed higher status.

Spice Box.description: A divided wooden or metal box for keeping costly spices secure and dry.

Aquamanile.description: A bronze or ceramic ewer in animal form (often a lion or knight) used for hand-washing at the table.

Wash Basin.description: A shallow brass or pewter bowl for washing hands or face, often paired with an ewer.

Reliquary Casket.description: A small ornamented chest of gilt copper, ivory, or enamelled metal containing a holy relic.

Andiron.description: A pair of iron firedogs that support burning logs in the hearth.

Pothook.description: An adjustable iron hook hung above the hearth fire to suspend pots at varying heights.

Trivet.description: A three- or four-legged iron stand placed over coals to support a pot or kettle.

Spit.description: A long iron rod turned over the fire to roast meat, sometimes powered by a turnspit dog or weighted gear.

Gridiron.description: A grilled iron frame for broiling meat or fish over an open fire.

Cauldron.description: A heavy iron cooking pot with a bail handle, suspended over the hearth fire.

Ale Jack.description: A blackened leather jug stiffened with pitch, used in taverns to serve beer.

Tankard.description: A cylindrical pewter or wooden drinking vessel with a hinged lid and a thumb-piece.

Linen Smock.description: A loose linen undergarment worn next to the skin by men and women alike.

Hose.description: Long fitted woollen leg-coverings tied to the braies with points.

Braies.description: Loose linen drawers reaching from waist to knee, the standard medieval underpants.

Wimple.description: A cloth covering for the head and neck worn by married women and nuns.

Coif.description: A close-fitting linen cap tied under the chin, worn by both sexes beneath other headgear.

Chaperon.description: A hood with a long liripipe tail, often draped fashionably over the shoulder.

Surcoat.description: A loose sleeveless overgarment worn over the cotte or armor, often emblazoned with arms.

Pattens.description: Wooden overshoes raised on platforms, worn over fine shoes to keep them clean from mud.

Liripipe Hood.description: A long-tailed cloth hood that may be wrapped around the head or shoulders.

Adze, Cooper's.description: A short curved adze used by coopers to shape barrel staves.

Croze.description: A specialised cooper's plane that cuts the groove for the barrel head.

Drawknife.description: A two-handled blade pulled toward the worker to shave wood.

Froe.description: An L-shaped splitting tool struck with a wooden mallet to cleave shingles or staves.

Plane, Wooden.description: A wooden joiner's plane with an iron blade for smoothing timber.

Mortise Chisel.description: A heavy chisel with a thick blade used for cutting rectangular mortises.

Mason's Trowel.description: A flat steel blade with a wooden handle used to spread mortar.

Drop Spindle.description: A weighted stick spun in midair to twist fibre into thread.

Fleshing Knife.description: A two-handled curved blade used to scrape fat and flesh from a hide.

Glassblower's Pipe.description: A long iron blowpipe used to gather and inflate molten glass.

Pax.description: A small panel of wood or metal kissed by the congregation in place of the kiss of peace.

Prie-dieu.description: A narrow kneeler with a sloped shelf used for private prayer.

Cope.description: A long ceremonial cloak worn by clergy in processions, often richly embroidered.

Maniple.description: A narrow band of cloth worn over the priest's left arm during Mass.

Vielle.description: A bowed five-stringed fiddle, the favourite instrument of medieval minstrels and troubadours.

Citole.description: A small flat-backed plucked instrument with four or five strings, popular at court.

Gittern.description: A small lute-like instrument carved from a single block of wood.

Psaltery.description: A trapezoidal plucked zither with strings stretched across a soundbox.

Crumhorn.description: A J-shaped wooden double-reed wind instrument with a buzzing tone.

Sackbut.description: An early trombone with a slide, used in late-medieval ceremonial music.

Tabor.description: A small double-headed drum slung at the waist and beaten with a single stick.

Tafl Set.description: A board with carved pieces for hnefatafl or a related Norse game of king-and-defenders.

Nine Men's Morris Board.description: A scratched or inlaid board for the popular medieval line-game also called merels.

Palmer's Staff.description: A long iron-shod staff carried by pilgrims, often topped with a gourd or scrip.

Travelling Cloak.description: A wide-cut woollen cloak with a hood, broad enough to wrap the sleeper at need.

Oilskin.description: A heavy linen cloth treated with linseed oil to shed rain.

Lantern, Horn.description: A folding tinned-iron lantern with translucent horn panes that shield the candle from wind.

Cresset.description: An iron basket on a pole or wall bracket holding a burning bundle of pitched rope.

Plough, Heavy.description: A wheeled mouldboard plough drawn by a team of oxen, capable of breaking heavy clay soil.

Flail.description: Two stout sticks joined by a leather thong, swung to thresh grain on the threshing floor.

Shepherd's Crook.description: A long staff with a curved iron or horn head used to catch a sheep by the leg.

Beehive Skep.description: A coiled-straw dome housing a colony of bees; the keeper smokes the hive to harvest honey.

Sieve.description: A wooden hoop with a stretched horsehair or wire mesh, used to sift flour or seed.

Steelyard Balance.description: An unequal-arm beam balance with a sliding counterweight, used by merchants for bulk goods.

Bill of Exchange.description: A written merchant's order to pay a sum at another city or fair; the seed of medieval banking.

Wax Seal Matrix.description: A carved metal die bearing the owner's device, pressed into hot wax to authenticate documents.

Indulgence.description: A printed letter granting remission of temporal punishment for sins, sold by pardoners.

Boar (domestic).description: A bristly black domestic pig kept for meat, lard, and bristles for brushes.

Lymer Hound.description: A scent hound led on a leash to track game silently before the hunt is unleashed.

Goshawk.description: A short-winged hunting hawk flown from the fist to take rabbits, hares, and pheasants.

Peregrine Falcon.description: A long-winged falcon flown at game birds; the favourite raptor of nobles.

Close-Stool.description: A boxed seat with a removable chamber pot, the private toilet of the wealthy.

Bathing Tub.description: A large oak tub, shaped like a half barrel, lined with linen and filled with hot water.

Strigil.description: A curved bronze blade used to scrape oil and dirt from the bather's skin.

Tooth Powder.description: A coarse mixture of cuttlefish bone, salt, and herbs, rubbed on the teeth with a cloth.

Ear-Pick.description: A slender silver tool, the spoon end for cleaning ears and the point for the teeth.
